title: Myths to correct
objectives: Correct five goal myths with the reality behind each.
Explain why “one big portfolio is enough” is wrong.
body_md:
“One big portfolio is enough; goals are just labels.” Reality: different goals need different time frames and asset mixes. “Long-term goals need the highest-return fund.” Reality: they need enough growth with a mix the client can hold through falls. “Short-term goals should be in equity for better returns.” Reality: money needed soon can't afford a market fall; it belongs in debt. “Once the plan is made, I'm done.” Reality: goals, costs and markets change; review every year. “Retirement is far away; I'll plan later.” Reality: it is usually the largest goal, and the one most hurt by a late start.

| Myth | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "One big portfolio is enough; goals are just labels." | Different goals need different time frames and asset mixes. |
| "Long-term goals need the highest-return fund." | They need enough growth with a mix the client can hold through falls. |
| "Short-term goals should be in equity for better returns." | Money needed soon can't afford a market fall; it belongs in debt. |
| "Once the plan is made, I'm done." | Goals, costs and markets change; review every year. |
| "Retirement is far away; I'll plan later." | It is usually the largest goal, and the one most hurt by a late start. |

> **Investor takeaway:** Judge your investments by whether your goals are on track, not by daily market moves.
example: “Retirement is far away”: it is usually the largest goal, and the one most hurt by a late start — ₹50,000 a month today is about ₹2.15 lakh a month in 25 years at 6% inflation.
say: Different goals need different time frames and asset mixes.
Retirement is usually the largest goal; don't plan it last.
never: One big portfolio is enough; goals are just labels.
Short-term goals should be in equity for better returns.

o: SEBI requires one rate per goal
